claim: Intel's 21 January 2022 press release announced an initial investment of more than US$20 billion to build two new leading-edge chip factories in Licking County, Ohio.
evidence: "Intel today announced plans for an initial investment of more than $20 billion in the construction of two new leading-edge chip factories in Ohio." (press release, 21 Jan 2022, p. 1)

metric.name: Intel Ohio initial investment as announced (two fabs)
metric.population: First two leading-edge fabs at the Licking County site

notes: Corrects CLM-2129: the January 2022 announcement was >US$20bn; the >US$28bn figure appears in Intel's later (Nov 2024) Ohio press kit, whose own photo captions still say 'more than $20 billion' for January 2022. Same release: site could reach up to US$100bn over the decade at full build-out.

claim: TSMC's FY2025 Form 20-F states that as of 28 February 2026 TSMC owned approximately 72.6% of the equity interest in JASM, after Sony, DENSO and Toyota took minority stakes.
evidence: "By way of such investment, Toyota also took a minority stake in JASM. As of February 28, 2026, we owned approximately 72.6% of the equity interest in JASM." (Form 20-F FY2025, Item 4, Organizational structure: JASM)

metric.name: TSMC equity interest in JASM
metric.population: TSMC's equity interest in Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing, Inc.
metric.methodology: Company disclosure in SEC annual report

notes: Confirms CLM-2117 (73% at end-2025) and shows the 86.5% planned in CLM-2123 was not the realised stake; the 20-F section opened does not explain the difference.

claim: TSMC's FY2025 Form 20-F still depreciates machinery and equipment over 5 years and buildings over 10 to 20 years on a straight-line basis.
evidence: "computed using the straight-line method mainly over the following estimated useful lives: land improvements - 10 to 20 years; buildings ... - 10 to 20 years; machinery and equipment ... - 5 years; and office equipment - 5 years." (Form 20-F FY2025, notes to consolidated financial statements, property, plant and equipment)
notes: Shows the 2020 policy in CLM-2118 is unchanged in the FY2025 filing (only land improvements changed from 20 years to 10-20 years).

claim: TSMC's first US fab is TSMC Washington (formerly WaferTech, Fab 11) in the State of Washington, set up as a joint venture in 1996, with commercial production from October 1998; TSMC owned 100% of it as of 28 February 2026.
evidence: "In 1996, we entered into a joint venture called WaferTech (of which the manufacturing entity is Fab 11) ... commercial production commenced in October 1998. In December 2023, WaferTech was renamed as TSMC Washington. As of February 28, 2026, we owned 100% of the equity interest in TSMC Washington." (Form 20-F FY2025, Item 4)
notes: Corrects the location in CLM-2140: the fab Morris Chang called the 'Oregon' factory is TSMC Washington (ex-WaferTech), whose land the 20-F places 'in the State of Washington in the United States'. It started as a joint venture in 1996, not 1997.
